lines: Best keep moving.
The road will not walk itself.
Keep your eyes open.
One road at a time.
There is always another turning.
Steel out.
Trouble. Ready yourself.
So be it.
They have chosen poorly.
It is done.
That was the last of them.
Still standing.
The road is quiet again.
Easy now.
One clean shot.
Hold steady.
Let the spell hold.
By the old arts.
Now, magicka answer me.
That struck deep.
I felt that.
Careful. Another like that will cost me.
I am badly hurt.
I need to mind my wounds.
I cannot take much more.
A healer. Quickly.
One more good blow may finish me.
I am at death's door.
Better.
Strength returns.
That will keep me on my feet.
I need a moment to breathe.
My legs are failing me.
I cannot keep this pace forever.
My magicka is nearly spent.
I have little spellcraft left in me.
I must husband what magicka remains.
Air. Now.
I need the surface.
My breath is nearly gone.
I carry too much.
This burden will slow me.
I should leave something behind.
Better. I can move again.
That is a burden shed.
Much lighter.
Keep a hand near your weapon.
Old stone, old dangers.
Few places like this are truly empty.
Let us see what waits below.
A roof and a market would be welcome.
Back among walls and watchmen.
Let us see what news travels here.
Open country again.
The Bay has long roads.
Best watch the horizon.
I know what is asked of me.
Another obligation, then.
Very well. I have a task.
That matter is behind me.
One obligation fewer.
So ends that errand.
That road is closed to me now.
I have failed that charge.
No use pretending otherwise. That task is lost.
There you are.
At last. The trail ends here.
Found you.
The contract is fulfilled.
That settles the matter.
The quarry is down.
I could use a proper meal.
It has been too long since I ate.
My stomach is beginning to complain.
I need food before I go farther.
Hunger is weakening me.
I will not last long without a meal.
I need water.
A clean drink would be welcome.
My mouth is dry as old parchment.
Soaked through.
These clothes will never dry at this rate.
I have had enough rain for one journey.
This cold is becoming dangerous.
I can scarcely feel my fingers.
I need warmth soon.
This heat is punishing.
Shade and water. Soon.
Even the road seems to shimmer.
This ground will serve.
A fire and a few hours' rest will do.
We make camp here.
Something warm at last.
A hot meal will put strength back in me.
Better than another mouthful of trail rations.
Night comes quickly on the road.
Best mind what moves after dark.
The light is going.
That rest did me good.
I am ready to move.
Strength enough for another road.
Poison. I need a remedy.
Something foul is in my blood.
I must cure this before it worsens.
I feel ill. This is no common weariness.
I should find a healer.
Something is wrong with me.
Then we are off.
Another road begins.
Best make good time.
At last.
We have arrived.
That is enough road for now.
The Iliac Bay has ambition, if not always refinement.
One grows accustomed to provincial habits.
Competence remains a rare and useful virtue.
Do not embarrass yourselves.
Very well. Let us settle the matter properly.
You mistake patience for weakness.
Predictable.
As expected.
They overestimated themselves.
Crude masonry. Let us hope its secrets are less disappointing.
Age does not make every ruin worthy.
At least the old disciplines endure.
A little proper sorcery.
Even discipline does not excuse an empty stomach.
I require something fit to eat.
What a miserable climate.
I was not bred for this dreary cold.
Let us see what passes for civility here.
Perhaps someone here keeps a respectable library.
This one keeps to the road.
Khajiit has walked stranger paths.
The moons see many roads, and so does this one.
Claws out, then.
This one warned you.
Khajiit is not easy prey.
This one still has all nine lives. More or less.
The foolish ones are quiet now.
Khajiit prefers victories that leave the fur intact.
This one does not trust the smell of this place.
Khajiit would rather have moonlight overhead.
This one would welcome something to eat.
Khajiit's stomach has begun making demands.
This one needs water before the road grows longer.
This one remembers warmer sands.
Cold gets beneath the fur all the same.
Where there are walls, there are purses and rumors.
This one wonders what the market holds.
The path changes. I change with it.
Still water may hide a deep channel.
I have crossed stranger ground than this.
Then let blood answer blood.
Come closer, if you choose.
The danger has passed.
Their struggle is finished.
Dry stone remembers little of living things.
The air here has been still too long.
The cold slows the blood.
I need warmth before my limbs grow stiff.
At least the water is familiar.
Others curse the rain. I have known worse.
The heat is heavy, even for me.
No sense standing about.
Forward, then.
A long road is still only a road.
Come on, then!
Steel speaks now.
Let's have it.
A good enough fight.
They should have brought more steel.
Done. Who is next?
This? I have known colder mornings.
A little frost never killed a Nord worth the name.
Stone, dust, and something waiting to die.
If there is treasure below, we earn it.
I could eat a whole roast by now.
Food first, heroics after.
I have endured worse roads than this.
Let us be done with it.
The west is loud, but rarely subtle.
You have chosen your end.
Very well. Come.
Fools die everywhere alike.
Finished.
Their ancestors may judge them now.
The dead are seldom the worst company in a ruin.
Old places breed old grudges.
Another western town. Let us hope its merchants are less dull than its walls.
Magic has older masters than these western hedge-wizards.
Keep your footing and your head.
The road rewards discipline.
A steady hand carries farther than boasting.
Stand ready.
Draw cleanly.
Let skill decide it.
Good. The matter is settled.
Poor form. Worse judgment.
A blade is honest about such things.
Breathe. Loose cleanly.
Measure the distance.
Watch the corners. Ruins favor the careless.
Patience. Stone hides more than treasure.
Let us see what trade and rumor have reached this place.
A town is only as useful as its people.
A charge accepted should be completed.
I gave my word. That is enough.
The road is kinder beneath an open sky.
Keep light on your feet.
There is always a trail, if you know how to look.
Too much stone. Not enough sky.
I dislike places where nothing grows.
Easy breath. Easy hand.
One arrow is enough.
Quiet again.
The trail is clear.
I should find something to eat before the trail lengthens.
Another turn in the road.
The Bay has a way of making every errand political.
Let us see where this leads.
Let us put the old arts to work.
A little sorcery may save a great deal of steel.
There will be a guildhall, a tavern, and three opinions for every fact.
Let us hear what the locals are whispering.
Very well. Another thread in the Bay's tangled affairs.
I will see it through.
Every old keep in High Rock seems to have a cellar full of trouble.
Stick around.
Let's pin this down.
Stay right there.
Anybody else?
Consider that settled.
You should have stayed at the tavern.
Now you see the magic trick.
A little theatrical sorcery.
Ice to meet you.
Cold enough for you?
You needed to cool your temper.
You're fired.
That should warm you up.
Ashes to ashes.
I've had worse.
Is that all you've got?
You'll have to do better than that.
Case closed.
Another happy ending. More or less.
That's one for the chronicles.
Contract fulfilled.
Consider yourself dismissed.
End of the line.
Very well. I will do it.
Agreed. I will see it done.
You have my help.
No. Find another hand.
I must decline.
That is not a charge I will take.
Yes.
Very well.
Agreed.
No.
Not this time.
I think not.
Guilty.
I plead guilty.
Not guilty.
I deny the charge.
Then hear my argument.
Allow me to make my case.
There is more to this than you have heard.
That is not how it happened.
You have been told the wrong tale.
Your account is mistaken.
This one accepts.
Khajiit will do what is asked.
This one will take the task.
This one must decline.
Khajiit has another road to walk.
Very well. I will see it done.
I suppose this task does require a capable hand.
Certainly not.
I have better uses for my time.
I will see it through.
The path is clear. I accept.
No. My path leads elsewhere.
I will not take this task.
Aye. I will do it.
Done. Point me where I need to go.
No. Find someone else.
Not my fight.
Agreed. I will see it done.
You have my word.
No. I will not take this charge.
My answer is no.
Very well. I accept.
Fine. I will handle it.
No. Trouble someone else.
I have no use for this errand.
All right. I will do it.
Agreed. I will see where the trail leads.
No. I will pass.
Find another traveler.
Very well. You have my help.
Agreed. I will take the task.
I must decline.
No. I cannot help you.
Lady Brisienna, then. Best not keep the Emperor's agent waiting.
The Emperor's charge still hangs over me. I should remember why I came to the Bay.
Daggerfall. Lysandus' shadow hangs over more than the castle walls.
Wayrest has enough wealth to make every smile look expensive.
Sentinel wears its pride openly. I should mind the customs of the court.
Privateer's Hold still smells of damp stone and bad luck.
My name carries obligations now, whether I asked for them or not.
The Guild has taught me that every locked door eventually becomes a question of method.
A Fighters Guild contract is simple enough: know the work, do the work, collect the fee.
Best not linger. Too many people know my name for the wrong reasons.
A good name opens doors that lockpicks cannot.
There is always more to understand.
Knowledge is useful only when one knows what to do with it.
Observe first. Conclusions can wait.
If reason has failed, then let discipline answer.
Enough. I will not let ignorance become violence without reply.
A poor lesson, but a lesson all the same.
Done. Better to remember why it came to blows.
Old places deserve caution. Their builders usually had reasons for closing the door.
Ruins keep knowledge long after they lose their keepers.
A settlement is a library written in habits instead of ink.
Listen long enough and every town explains itself.
Rumor is unreliable, but patterns survive even bad telling.
A tavern can teach as much about a town as its archives.
Faith preserves memories scholarship often neglects.
Ritual can outlive the reason that first created it.
Institutions remember what individuals forget.
A guild hall is useful when its members still value the craft.
The land has its own history, even where no one bothered to write it down.
There are older lessons beneath open sky than in many towers.
I will see this through, and understand what I can along the way.
Very well. Better a difficult truth than an easy assumption.
Another question answered. Usually that only reveals the next one.
The matter is settled. I should remember what it taught me.
Pain is persuasive, if not particularly subtle.
That was an argument I would rather not hear twice.
Wisdom now means finding a healer.
I have learned enough about this wound already.
A tired mind makes careless judgments.
I need rest before exhaustion starts deciding for me.
My reserves are nearly spent. Time for restraint.
No sense proving a theorem with an empty well of magicka.
Even scholarship fares poorly on an empty stomach.
Water first. Thought becomes very small when the body is neglected.
Cold dulls the hands before it dulls the mind. I should warm both.
Night hides detail. That makes observation more important, not less.
Form, intent, release.
Let the old principles hold true once more.
Measure distance. Then loose.
Every road is an argument about where the world connects.
Arrival is the useful part. Now I can learn why this place matters.
Poison is alchemy with malicious intent. I still need an antidote.
Symptoms first, panic later. I need a healer.
The timid call knowledge forbidden when they fear its price.
Power leaves traces. I have learned to notice them.
Every prohibition tells me where someone buried a secret.
Blood is such an old currency.
You have chosen to contribute to the experiment.
Death is informative when one bothers to study it.
Another silence. Sometimes silence is useful.
Sealed places attract me for excellent reasons and everyone else for terrible ones.
If something was buried here, I want to know why it frightened them.
Civilized streets conceal the same hungers as tombs. They merely dress them better.
Wine loosens tongues. Fear loosens them faster.
Priests guard mysteries with ceremony and call curiosity a sin.
Sacred places are often old power wrapped in better ceremony.
Guild rules exist to keep lesser minds from touching dangerous things.
There are places beyond law where useful rites leave fewer witnesses.
If this leads somewhere interesting, I will indulge it.
Very well. Let us see what this task is really hiding.
Useful. The cost was acceptable.
One mystery closed, and perhaps a more profitable one opened.
Pain is temporary. Lessons endure.
Not yet. I have too much left to uncover.
The body complains. It will obey a little longer.
Annoying. Power without reserves is only theory.
The flesh insists on its petty maintenance.
I require water. Even ambition has a body attached to it.
Cold preserves corpses better than patience preserves secrets.
Night improves the world. Fewer witnesses, clearer intentions.
Power answers those willing to command it.
Distance makes the result no less final.
If the road ends somewhere forbidden, so much the better.
At last. Let us see what everyone else was afraid to touch.
A crude poison. I refuse to die from someone else's unimaginative work.
Disease is merely another process to master before it masters me.
Courtesy reveals more than aggression ever does.
A good name opens doors force only damages.
People remember how they were treated.
There was still time to choose civility. They wasted it.
A needless end to a conversation that never began.
Places like this punish arrogance. Caution is not cowardice.
New streets, new customs. Best learn both before judging either.
If I want the truth of a town, I should listen to the people who work after court closes.
Respect costs nothing, especially in another people's sacred place.
Every guild has rules, rivalries, and someone whose opinion matters more than their title suggests.
No walls, no court, no audience. A useful change.
You have my word. I will treat the matter seriously.
Good. Let the people concerned have some peace from it.
That was an emphatic rejection.
Pride will not stop the bleeding. I need help.
I need to recover before exhaustion makes me careless with people or danger.
I have little magicka left. Persuasion may have to do the work.
A meal and a civilized table would be welcome.
I would settle for water and five quiet minutes.
Hospitality suddenly sounds less ceremonial and more essential.
At night, intentions become harder to read. I should watch more closely.
Power is most useful when applied with restraint.
One warning would have been preferable.
The road is easier when one leaves a place with friends rather than grudges.
We are here. First impressions matter.
Someone has made this personal. I need an antidote before I ask who.
I should find a healer before I become someone else's problem.
Authority is wasted on those who mistake inheritance for merit.
The world belongs to those capable of imposing order upon it.
Let lesser people debate permission.
You presume far beyond your station.
Order restored.
Someone once commanded this place. Now it waits for a worthier will.
Every town has a ruler. The interesting question is whether they deserve the obedience.
Useful places. Men confess their loyalties cheaply over drink.
Even gods require institutions to enforce their importance.
A hierarchy is only as strong as the person at its summit.
No throne in sight. The land remains subject to whoever can hold it.
Very well. I will decide how this matter ends.
As expected. The matter yielded to competence.
Insolent.
I will not be reduced to carrion by this place.
The body grows tiresome. The will does not.
My power is diminished, not my authority.
Find food. There is no dignity in being ruled by an empty stomach.
I require water, not a lesson in humility.
A miserable climate for people who expect to be obeyed.
Darkness changes nothing. Predators remain predators.
Obey.
Kneeling would have been simpler.
Let the road carry me to someone worth dealing with.
At last. Let us meet whoever imagines they hold power here.
Poison. The weapon of someone too frightened to stand before me.
An indignity. I will have it cured.
Do the work in front of you.
Courage is easier when you remember who depends on it.
A promise should mean something.
Stand fast.
You wanted a fight. Face me.
It is finished. Check the wounded.
Enough blood for one day.
Stay alert. Places like this punish carelessness.
Whatever waits below, we meet it ready.
Walls are only worthwhile if the people behind them can sleep safely.
A meal, a drink, and then back to the road.
No harm in showing respect where others place their faith.
A hall means little without people willing to stand for one another.
Open ground. Keep watch and keep moving.
You have my word. I will see it done.
The charge is fulfilled.
Still standing.
I need treatment, not bravado.
Slow down. Exhaustion gets good people killed.
Then steel will have to suffice.
I fight better fed. Simple truth.
Water first. No heroics against thirst.
Keep moving. Cold wins when you stop.
Night watch starts now.
Let it strike true.
Make the shot count.
We have a road and a purpose. That is enough.
We made it. Now find who needs us.
Poison. Find a cure before it takes my strength.
I need a healer. Duty is no excuse for spreading sickness.
Fair fights are for people who failed to find an advantage.
If it is guarded, someone thinks it is valuable.
Locks are just opinions made of metal.
You should have watched your back.
Expensive mistake on their part.
Dark, dangerous, probably full of things nobody is using anymore.
New streets. New purses. New patrol routes.
Now this is civilization: ale, loose tongues, and terrible judgment.
Donation boxes always have the most trusting locks.
Every guild has a back door, even when the members pretend otherwise.
No guards for miles. Pity there is not much worth stealing either.
If the reward is real, so am I.
Done. Now for the part where someone pays me.
That was my cue to stop fighting fairly.
Time to disappear before courage becomes stupidity.
Running out of breath is a terrible way to get caught.
No magicka. Fine. I still have hands and bad intentions.
Hard to rob anyone when my stomach announces me first.
A tavern would solve at least one of my problems.
Frozen fingers are useless on locks.
Finally. The respectable people are going home.
A spell is just another lockpick if you use it correctly.
They cannot catch what they never reach.
Let us hope the destination has richer people than the road.
Good. Time to learn where they keep the valuable things.
Poison? Rude. Effective, but rude.
Wonderful. Even my blood is trying to report me.
People matter more than the stories told about them.
Kindness is rarely wasted.
A little decency travels farther than most people think.
Leave them alone.
I asked you not to make this necessary.
I wish it had ended another way.
I wonder how many people never came home from places like this.
Good. People, lights, and somewhere warm.
A warm room full of stories sounds just right.
Whatever god they pray to, someone comes here needing hope.
Groups are only worth joining if they remember the people inside them.
Beautiful country. Lonely, though.
If someone needs help, I cannot simply walk away.
Good. I hope that leaves someone better off than before.
That hurt. I would still rather be hit than watch someone else take it.
I need help. No shame in saying it.
I need a rest before I become a burden to anyone.
I have little magicka left. I should save it for when someone truly needs it.
A simple meal would be enough.
Water would be wonderful right now.
I hope anyone else on this road has found shelter.
Someone is probably waiting for a traveler who has not come home yet.
Let this do some good.
I would rather they turned away.
One more road. We will get there together.
At last. I hope we are welcome.
I need a cure before this gets worse.
Best find a healer, and keep my distance from others until I do.
Everyone has a breaking point. The interesting part is finding it.
People are so much more honest when they are afraid.
A little chaos keeps life from becoming dull.
Good. I was getting bored.
That was almost entertaining.
Dark, miserable, probably lethal. Charming.
So many rules in one place. Where to begin?
Drink makes people brave, stupid, and wonderfully easy to provoke.
All that virtue gathered in one room. Tempting.
Rules, ranks, little badges of importance. Adorable.
No witnesses. The countryside improves already.
Why not? Perhaps someone interesting will suffer.
And everyone lived happily ever after. Except the ones who did not.
Oh, now you have my attention.
Careful. I am much less pleasant when cornered.
Even cruelty becomes work eventually.
No magicka left. We will improvise.
I am hungry. Someone nearby should probably be nervous.
I need a drink. Preferably somewhere with fragile furniture.
Cold enough to make everyone miserable. Lovely.
The dark makes honest people imagine such wonderful things.
Let us make this memorable.
Hold still. Or do not. Either way is funny.
A new road, a new collection of mistakes waiting to happen.
Here we are. Let us ruin the local peace.
Someone tried poison. I almost respect the effort.
How undignified. I prefer suffering with an audience.
There is always another road worth taking.
If nobody has a good story about the place, I suppose I will have to make one.
The map gets interesting where the certainty ends.
I was hoping for a quieter tour.
Still worth the trip.
Now this is why I left the road.
Old door, bad air, terrible idea. Naturally I am going in.
New town. First find the landmarks, then find the trouble.
Every good journey deserves one bad tavern story.
You learn a lot about a place from what its people build for the gods.
Local experts. Useful when the map stops helping.
This is the part no court map ever gets quite right.
Sounds like a journey. I am in.
That one will be worth telling later.
I have had smoother expeditions.
Adventure stops being charming when you bleed this much.
I need a rest before the next hill becomes the one that stops me.
Low on magicka. Good thing curiosity weighs nothing.
I have crossed enough country to earn a meal.
Find water. Then find the next road.
I have seen better climates and worse decisions.
The road looks different after dark. Usually more interesting.
Let us see if this gets us through.
Distance, wind, and one chance.
Now we are getting somewhere.
Worth the miles. Now what did we come all this way to find?
Of course the interesting route had poison.
I would rather not bring this home as a souvenir.
The rarest things usually belong to people who cannot appreciate them.
A locked door is a list of possessions waiting to change hands.
History is much easier to value when you can hold it.
You are standing between me and something I intend to possess.
Good. Now back to what actually matters.
Someone went to considerable trouble to keep people out. Promising.
Every old town has collectors, smugglers, and someone desperate to sell an heirloom.
Collectors talk when they drink. So do thieves who robbed them.
Temples accumulate relics with extraordinary consistency.
Guild archives often contain maps they have no intention of sharing.
Civilization ends. Buried things do not.
If the task crosses something rare, I want first look.
The job is finished. I hope the spoils were not disappointing.
Careful. I have not collected enough to die yet.
No artifact is worth bleeding out before I can take it home.
Treasure is inconveniently heavy after the tenth mile.
No magicka. Then I will use keys, tools, or other people's mistakes.
I can admire relics after I eat.
Water first. Dusty tombs are overrated on an empty throat.
Frozen ruins preserve valuables nicely. Less so fingers.
Darkness hides entrances. It also hides collectors.
Open.
I would rather not damage anything valuable behind you.
There had better be something worth bringing back.
At last. Now show me what this place has been hiding.
Ancient defenses or modern jealousy? Either way, irritating.
I refuse to let a ruin keep me by infecting me.
Do the job cleanly and move on.
Preparation turns danger into work.
Competence is quieter than bravado.
All right. Professional terms are over.
Job done.
Check the exits, check the floor, then worry about the monsters.
Find supplies, information, and whoever is paying.
Food, information, and perhaps a contract. Efficient.
If they heal wounds and answer questions, I do not need to share the theology.
Professionals usually keep records. Useful.
Travel light, keep bearings, and do not waste daylight.
Understood. I will handle it.
Contract complete.
Noted. Adjust.
Too injured to work properly. Fix that first.
Fatigue ruins technique. Time to rest.
Reserve nearly gone. Change methods.
Eat before hunger becomes a tactical problem.
Water now. Delays become mistakes.
Cold compromises grip and judgment. Find shelter.
Visibility down. Risk up.
Controlled release.
One shot. No waste.
Route set. Move.
We are on site. Start assessing.
Identify it, treat it, continue.
Symptoms are work conditions. Find a cure.
Someone always knows more than they admit.
Watch the hands, then the exits.
If the trail looks easy, someone may want it followed.
There you are.
One less set of tracks to worry about.
Too many blind corners. Somebody built this for ambushes whether they meant to or not.
New town. Find the guards, the gates, and who watches strangers.
Bounties start in places like this. So do traps.
Even honest people lie when sanctuary is involved.
A guild keeps lists. Lists mean names. Names mean leads.
Open ground shows tracks. It also shows mine.
Give me the facts. I will find the rest.
Trail ends here. For now.
They knew where to hit. Remember that.
Wounded means predictable. I need to stop being predictable.
Tired hunters miss signs. Rest.
If they are counting on my magic, let them.
Hunger makes noise. Eat before it gives me away.
Dry mouth, slower judgment. Fix it.
Cold hides tracks and slows hands. Bad combination.
Night is when both hunter and quarry start inventing ghosts.
Let them wonder where that came from.
Do not give them a second warning.
Check the trail behind us as often as the one ahead.
We arrived. Now find out who noticed.
Poison means planning. Someone wanted distance from the kill.
Could be bad luck. I do not rely on that explanation.
Daggerfall has scholars enough to record a king's death, but not enough certainty to quiet his ghost.
A murdered king and a city full of frightened stories. Death has fertile ground here.
Daggerfall's court is grieving, proud, and watched. Every word will travel.
A throne unsettled by one dead king is a throne that was never secure.
Lysandus was a warrior-king. Whatever haunts this city deserves a straight answer.
A royal city in mourning means distracted guards and nervous nobles.
Too many people here still speak of Lysandus like the grief happened yesterday.
A dead king screaming through the streets. Daggerfall knows how to entertain.
Daggerfall at last. Big walls, old harbor, and enough rumors to fill the road back out.
Royal cities collect royal relics. Grief makes people careless with inventories.
Daggerfall. Keep the job separate from the court drama until the court drama becomes the job.
A dead king, an uneasy court, and too many people insisting they know nothing. Someone does.
Wayrest grew wealthy by learning how to make trade serve ambition. That kind of lesson travels.
Wayrest polishes everything, even its secrets. Especially its secrets.
Wayrest is a court where commerce and etiquette share the same table.
Wayrest understands that wealth is only impressive when it can command obedience.
Wayrest looks comfortable. Comfortable courts can still breed dangerous orders.
Wayrest has money enough to make caution a profession.
For all the courtly games, ordinary people still have to live beneath them.
Everyone here smiles like there is a knife behind the teeth.
Wayrest sits where roads and ambitions meet. No wonder everyone passes through.
A rich court accumulates rare things simply to prove it can.
Wayrest pays well when it wants something handled quietly.
Too much wealth, too many factions. Perfect conditions for someone to disappear on purpose.
Sentinel preserves old traditions with more discipline than many Breton courts preserve records.
Old customs often hide old prohibitions. Those are usually worth studying.
Sentinel remembers courtesy and insult with equal precision.
Sentinel respects strength, lineage, and ceremony. At least they understand the language of rule.
Sentinel respects a person who stands by their word. Good.
Honor makes people predictable. Predictability is useful.
Pride can be harsh, but it also means people care deeply about what they inherit.
Everyone here takes honor so seriously. That makes offense wonderfully easy.
Sentinel feels different from the Breton kingdoms the moment the road turns dry.
Hammerfell has relics older than half the claims made about them. I would like to see the originals.
Sentinel values competence and clear terms. I can work with that.
In a place ruled by honor, accusations become weapons. Watch who points first.
Privateer's Hold is hardly ancient scholarship, but even crude places reveal how their occupants expected trouble.
The first hole I crawled from in the Bay. Every beginning deserves a little blood.
An unpleasant reminder that survival comes before ceremony.
Privateer's Hold. A fitting place for the world to learn it failed to kill me.
I survived this place once. I know better than to underestimate it now.
Smugglers and privateers rarely build empty rooms without a reason.
I wonder who else woke down here without knowing whether they would see daylight again.
